newsitem.title: JAMAICA: Caricom admits Haiti as newest member.
newsitem.headline: Caricom admits Haiti as newest member.

text.p: The 14-member Caribbean Community (Caricom) announced on Thursday it admitted Haiti as the newest full member, just days after agreeing to create a Caricom single market by 1999.
Caricom's chairman, Jamaican Prime Minister P.J. Patterson, called it a "historic decision," while Haitian President Rene Preval characterized it as a "great priviledge and a big step for Haiti."
Patterson said he expected that the final agreement would be ready for signing when Caricom leaders meet again in February or March in Grenada.

Preval, speaking in both French and English, said Haiti was "ready to consider all the conditions necessary to participate in the Caricom (single) market," although Patterson added the pace at which Haiti phases in the various provisions is still to be determined.
The decision to admit Haiti came just two months after it applied, even though a similar application from the British Virgin Islands has yet to be approved.

It also reversed a policy position taken four years ago to only accept the smaller states into Caricom, and restrict the larger countries, like Haiti, to joining the 24-nation Association of Caribbean States, which held its first summit in 1995. Haiti is a member of the ACS.

The admission of Haiti more than doubles Caricom's total population overnight, as Haiti's estimated seven million inhabitants exceeds the total of the remaining 14 Caricom states, which is six million.
Both Preval and Patterson said increased cooperation between Haiti and the rest of Caricom is expected to further strengthen Haiti's democratic institutions.

Preval noted Caricom's involvement in the peacekeeping forces that ousted Gen. Raoul Cedras in 1995 and its subsequent and continuing assistance to Haiti in a number of areas. Patterson stated this cooperation "will lead to the sort of peace, security and stability that is a prerequisite for economic growth."
With Haiti's inclusion, Caricom now counts as members the two countries, the other being Guyana, with the lowest per capita gross domestic products in the hemisphere.
Caricom began 24 years ago as a common market of former British colonies.
